articles.title: Analysis-Israel's election may change its leader, but not Iran war policy
articles.description: By Samia NakhoulDUBAI, Oct 21 (Reuters) - Israel's election next week may change its leader, but not its strategy: Iran will remain its chief adversary, military force will continue to be its preferred tool and Palestinian statehood a distant prospect, regional policymakers and analysts say.That is because the strategic assumptions underpinning Israeli policy were hardened by the October 7, 2023, attacks on southern Israeli communities by Palestinian militant group Hamas andby the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

articles.title: US is reducing staffing at 4 Middle East embassies over increased threats from Iran
articles.description: The State Department says it will reduce staffing at four U.S. embassies in the Middle East after receiving intelligence that Iran has stepped up efforts to target American personnel in the region and elsewhere. In a memo sent Friday to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said his teams “have received intelligence that Iran has substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel.” The memo was obtained by The Associated Press and reported earlier by Axios. It emerged shortly after the State Department announced that it's reducing staff at embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. Two U.S. officials said the Iran threat is related to the staffing changes.

articles.title: On October 23, 1983, 241 US marines died in a terrorist attack in Lebanon. It was the deadliest single-day loss for US forces since WWII
articles.description: On October 23, 1983, a truck bomb exploded at the Marine barracks in Beirut, killing 241 American servicemen. This attack occurred during Lebanon's civil war, where US troops were part of a peacekeeping mission. The bombing was attributed to Islamic Jihad, which opposed American presence in Lebanon. The devastating loss prompted a reassessment of US military operations and eventually led to troop withdrawal in 1984.
